SYNC WORKFLOW — AFTER ANY IN-GAME KEYBIND CHANGE
1. Save keybinds in game (writes a new layout_*_exported.xml)

2. Run "SC Sync All.bat" in Claude Stream Deck Project → Tools — updates the VoiceAttack profile + MASTER_KEYBINDS.json and prints the Stream Deck change report

3. Only if the report shows a changed action that maps to a deck button: rebuild the deck in the planner, pulling keys from MASTER_KEYBINDS.json (all_keyboard_binds)

4. Import the new .streamDeckProfile by double-clicking it with Stream Deck running — but QUIT Stream Deck first if overwriting files directly in ProfilesV3
RELEASE CHANNEL
HAULING — FIELD MANUAL
TIPS & TRICKS
• Fresh shard first (server-hop) = fewer cargo desync bugs; check Shard Health on the System page.
• Test a freight elevator empty before loading — cargo can vanish on a reset.
• Autoload for contracts; manual tractor for commodities you bought.
• The Hull series retracts its cargo spine to fly/land, extends it to load — it is not dock-only. What differs per ship is how you load it (table below).
• Buy low / sell high — compare prices on the Hauling commodities list / UEX.
HOW-TO GUIDE
A. DOCK AT A STATION
1. Fly within 5–7 km of the station.
2. Open Comms → Landing Services → Request.
3. ATC assigns a pad / docking port / hangar by ship size.
4. Docking port: align until the ring + lines turn green (circle to SE, lines centered), then grow the square to match the circle.
5. Press [ N ] (default) to invoke docking — clamps engage.
B. REQUEST / WITHDRAW CARGO
Freight elevators are in hangars, station cargo decks, distribution-centre wings, and some outposts.
1. Look at the Freight Elevator terminal (no keybind — on-screen console).
2. Withdraw items from local inventory onto the cargo grid.
NOTE: for a hauling contract, the contracted cargo already shows on the terminal.
C. THREE WAYS CARGO GETS LOADED
1. CONTRACT AUTOLOAD: on a hauling contract the freight elevator already holds the cargo — pull your ship; at the destination the terminal auto-collects it → submit the contract.
2. MANUAL (by hand): for commodities you bought, or a ship parked at a station cargo deck, raise the cargo on the elevator and tractor-beam each SCU box onto your grid yourself (MaxLift / multi-tool; the ATLS exosuit is fastest).
3. PAID AUTO-LOAD: if the ship is in your hangar, you can pay a fee to have it loaded/unloaded for you instead of hand-loading. [community: ~10,000 aUEC load+unload; availability varies by site — not every ship/location offers it, and big freighters (Hull-C) load at the external station elevator.]
TIP: test the elevator empty first — if it resets with cargo on the grid, the cargo can vanish.
C2. BUYING & SELLING COMMODITIES
Buy: purchase at a commodity kiosk → the SCU is credited at that location → withdraw it onto the freight elevator / cargo grid → load onto your ship (manual, or paid auto-load if it's in your hangar).
Sell: land/dock at the buyer → unload onto the freight elevator/terminal → the sale registers and you're paid.
NOTE: small ships often load right at a pad's elevator; big freighters route through the large external elevators on a station cargo deck.
D. UNDOCK / DEPART
1. Retract landing gear ([ N ] default).
2. Press [ N ] (default) to undock / request departure.
Hangar takeoff: no turntable — come to a hover and yaw 180° to face the doors, then fly out on ATC clearance.
E. HOW EACH SHIP LOADS (this is about LOADING access — not whether it can land)
ShipLoads viaNote
Hull-A / Hull-BLand + tractor / small elevatorSet down at outposts & pads; extend the cargo spine to load
Hull-CStation berth (spindle deployed)Can land (travel config — spindle retracted INSIDE the hull), but it can't load on its gear: the spindles are stowed inside. To load/unload it must deploy the spindle at a station berth + external freight elevator.
Hull-D / Hull-ENot flyable yet (4.8)Concept/lineup only — don't plan around them
C2 / M2 / A2 HerculesLand + pad/hangar elevatorPlanetary heavy cargo
CaterpillarLand + tractorModular freighter
Freelancer / Taurus / Cutlass / MSR / CorsairLand + tractor / elevatorSmall–medium haulers land at pads & outposts
Verified 4.8 (starcitizen.tools): Hull-C is no longer dock-only — it's shown landed/stored in hangars, and its folding cargo spindle (retract to fly, extend to load) is a real component. Hull-C open planet-surface landing is unconfirmed. Hull-D/E aren't confirmed flyable. The real per-ship difference is loading access (freight-elevator size / land-and-tractor), not landing.
F. TIPS & TRICKS
• Hull-C config [4.8 verified]: it folds the cargo spindle IN to fly/land (stores in an XL hangar) and OUT to load. KEY: it can't load while sitting on its landing gear — in landed config the spindles are stowed inside the hull, so loading/unloading only happens when it deploys the spindle at a station berth (external freight elevator). So it lands fine (not dock-only), but loading is station-only. Open planet-surface landing still unconfirmed.
• Squeeze extra SCU [community — risky]: loading MANUALLY by tractor beam, you can sometimes stack more than the rated SCU into open space as long as the grid isn't fully gridlocked (auto-snapped). Unsecured boxes can spill or despawn on a quantum jump or hard maneuver — not for valuable cargo.
• Move ONE box at a time [4.8 verified bug]: moving multiple items at once can desync inventory and lock the screen — transfer cargo singly.
• Fresh shard first: server-hop (log out/in) before a big haul; higher Server FPS = fewer cargo desync bugs. Check Shard Health (button on the System page) first.
• External elevators: use them where available and test empty first — if the grid resets with cargo on it, the cargo can vanish.
• Argo ATLS [community]: the ATLS loading exosuit speeds manual load/unload dramatically.
• Short loops stack: a 30k / 10-min run beats a 70k / 40-min run per hour. Confirm stock, price, demand and SELL capacity in the current server before loading a big hold — demand caps can strand cargo.
• Keep a reserve: keep 30–50% of your aUEC OUT of cargo so a lost run doesn't wipe you.
• Top off quantum fuel before long hauls; heavy, full ships burn more.

A Note to CIG
I’m one person building this in the open, and getting to work with CIG on a small read-only, opt-in surface would be a dream. A studio this size has no shortage of priorities, so I’m not expecting a solo project to jump the queue — I’d rather let the work earn the conversation. If CmdGlas helps new players find their feet a little faster and aids veterans in accomplishing mission tasks, I hope that’s a reason worth a reply.

The shape of the ask matters. Not a cloud API – that is a server bill and an account-security argument. A local, read-only, opt-in surface. The game is already running on this PC. A player-consented localhost endpoint exposing state the client already holds in memory would collapse nearly all of the manual workarounds below. No servers, no account exposure, and no write path, therefore no anti-cheat surface – which is the objection that kills most ideas like this one.

This map slot is empty because the official starmap cannot be embedded. That is the small version of a much bigger thing.

CmdGlas is built entirely from the outside. Everything below is something the game already knows and this tablet has to reverse-engineer off the screen. Not a wish list – every one is a workaround living in this codebase right now:
  • A build / version endpoint.Smallest ask, biggest payoff. On 2026-07-16 the 4.9 release notes said the launcher shows 4.9.0-LIVE.1825000, while the community datamine said 12232306. The datamine is almost certainly right: build ids climb monotonically (…11825000 → 11952564 → 12030094 → 12232306), and 1825000 is 4.8.0's 11825000 missing its leading digit – it would be lower than every build since 4.5.0. So a tablet reading the notes would have shown the wrong build, and only arithmetic caught it. One authoritative field would end that entire class of guessing.
  • Live keybind state.Today it needs a manual profile export, then the tablet reads the newest layout_*_exported.xml. That file holds 67 joystick binds this rig actually uses – VKB, VIRPIL, rudder – and a keybind tool still struggles to see them. The game has them live.
  • Read-only shard / server identity.Shard health is currently obtained by screenshotting the in-game r_displayInfo overlay and having the tablet read the text off it. That is the honest state of the art from out here.
  • Inventory and loadout, read-only.Inventory is presently typed into a notepad and read back out. You are the data source.
  • Authoritative item data.The community datamine lies by omission: 4.9's Bellator / BUL-H4 super-heavy set reports sub_type_label: "Heavy". Only the raw damage multiplier (0.125 against 0.60) reveals it is a new tier. Trust the obvious field and you ship a wrong answer.
  • Live scan data.Ore quality is a number you read off the HUD and type in by hand. The 4.9 scanning changes give you more to read and still nothing to read from.
  • Terminal prices.Currently user-reported via UEX – this tablet's own footer admits older data should be treated as suspect.
  • An embeddable map.The reason you are reading this on an empty page.
That promise is already kept in the other direction: this tool never writes to a game file. Not the keybind list, not the install – verified against its own source code, not merely asserted. The only files it ever creates are peripheral binding profiles, in their own folders, when you ask it to. Read-only is what it wants and read-only is all it wants.

Every figure in this tablet is second-hand, so it is tagged VERIFIED / COMMUNITY / UNCONFIRMED – because guessing would be worse than admitting the gap.

Until then it stays unofficial, unaffiliated, and honest about what it does not know.
Found one worth embedding? Hand me the URL and it goes here.

SALVAGE
SALVAGE — FIELD MANUAL
TIPS & TRICKS
• Blue hull sections are richest — scrape those first.
• Steady distance and angle beats upgrades for scrape speed.
• Master RMC (hull scraping) before moving to structural / CM.
• Grab loose components / cargo with a tractor beam for extra income.
• Vulture = solo single wrecks; Reclaimer = big multi-crew jobs.
HOW-TO GUIDE
A. SETUP & APPROACH
1. Find a wreck — Salvage contracts (Contract Manager), reclaim missions, or free-fly wrecks.
2. Pick the ship: Drake Vulture (solo, single wrecks), Aegis Reclaimer (large / multi-crew fleets).
3. Enter Salvage Mode (default [ M ]) and face the hull. RMB aims the beam(s); mouse wheel adjusts beam gap/focus.
B. HULL SCRAPING → RMC
1. In scrape mode, hold LMB and sweep the beam across the hull.
2. Read the panel outline: blue = rich, yellow = mediocre, red = nearly depleted.
3. Keep a stable distance and angle, work in zones, avoid chaotic boosting — technique beats upgrades for scrape speed.
4. Scraped material becomes RMC (Recycled Material Composite) in your ship's filler.
C. STRUCTURAL SALVAGE → CM ("munching")
1. Once the hull is stripped, switch to the disintegration / structural sub-mode.
2. Break down the remaining structure — this yields Construction Materials (CM).
NOTE: CM is the bigger industrial step. New to salvage? Master RMC scraping first, add CM once stable.
D. STORE, PACKAGE & SELL
1. The Filler forms RMC/CM into SCU boxes (Reclaimer fillers package 2 / 8 / 16 SCU).
2. Haul the boxes to a Trade / Commodity terminal and sell RMC / CM — check the Hauling tab / UEX for best price.
3. Loose components / cargo on the wreck: grab with a tractor beam (multi-tool / ATLS) and sell separately.
E. HAND SALVAGE
Small wrecks / stray panels: use the multi-tool + Cambio-SRT salvage attachment on foot — faster than repositioning a ship for stragglers.
NOTE: In-game keybinds shown are CIG defaults — verify yours on the Keybinds page.
MINING — FIELD MANUAL
TIPS & TRICKS
• Scan from a distance to read a rock's mass and composition % before you commit.
• Higher mass = more yield but needs more power / a bigger laser (or multi-crew MOLE).
• Keep the energy bar in the green; if it creeps toward red, back away — distance lowers power.
• Quantanium is the big earner but destabilizes over time — refine/sell it promptly.
• Refined ore usually sells for more than raw — refine, then check prices on the Hauling tab.
• Stubborn rock? Fit modules that cut resistance / instability.
HOW-TO GUIDE
A. FIND & SCAN
1. Fly to a mining area — asteroid cluster, planet/moon surface, or a cave for hand mining.
2. Use Scanning Mode (default [ V ]) to locate deposits, or just approach visible rocks.
3. Look at a rock to read its MASS (kg) and, up close, its mineral composition %.
NOTE: Mass class sets the tool — see the MASS REFERENCE table below.
B. FRACTURE — THE POWER WINDOW
1. Enter Mining Mode (default [ M ]).
2. Confirm FRACTURE mode — rock outline is yellow (= crack). Toggle fracture/extract with Left Alt + LMB.
3. Hold LMB to fire; raise power by scrolling the mouse wheel UP slowly.
4. Drive the rock's energy bar into the GREEN optimal window and hold it there.
CAUTION: Do NOT let the bar fill into the RED overcharge zone — the rock explodes and the yield is lost.
5. If it spikes toward red, lower power or back away (distance cuts effective power). Do not try to save it with more laser.
C. EXTRACT
1. After the rock fractures into chunks, switch to EXTRACT (Left Alt + LMB) — chunk outline turns purple.
2. Hold LMB to draw ore into your ship/backpack until the chunk is depleted.
3. Repeat per chunk. Full cargo/canister → head to a refinery.
D. REFINE & SELL
1. Dock at a refinery (e.g. an ARC-L / refinery deck) and use the Refinery Terminal.
2. Select your ore. The terminal lists every method side-by-side with its YIELD %, TIME, and COST — those change per material, so compare before you commit. Methods (yield ↔ speed ↔ cost tradeoff):
• Dinyx Solventation — highest yield, but slowest (long real-time timer). Best started before you log off.
• Pyrometric Chromalysis — above-average yield; higher cost, slow.
• Ferron Exchange — balanced compromise of yield / fee / time. Safe default.
• Electrostarolysis, Gaskin Process, Kazen Winnowing, Thermonatic Deposition, XCR Reaction — mid-range; yield/time/cost vary by ore — read the terminal.
• Cormack Method — fastest + cheapest, but lowest yield. Use when you need it now or the ore is cheap.
CAUTION: no method is best for everything — higher yield usually means slower + pricier. A refinery calculator (UEX) can pre-compute the best method + yield per ore.
3. Pay, wait for the timer, then collect refined SCU onto a hauler.
4. Sell refined ore at a Trade / Commodity terminal — check the Hauling tab / UEX for best price. Use the YIELD ESTIMATOR below to value a rock before you crack it.
NOTE: In-game keybinds shown are CIG defaults — verify yours on the Keybinds page. No danger to you; the only loss is an over-charged rock.

SALVAGE PIN REFERENCE · what the scan number means
WHAT THIS IS: when you point at something to salvage in game, a marker (a “pin”) shows a number over it. That number means a different thing depending on what you are looking at — a whole wreck, a loose panel, a cargo crate, and so on.
HOW TO USE IT: find your target in the first column, then read across — what the number is telling you, which tool to use, and roughly what you’ll get.
MINING OR SALVAGE? if you see a “STRONG / WEAK” strength bar and a 90° angle widget on the pin, you are in mining mode and the number is rock mass. No strength bar = salvage mode, and this table applies.

WHAT THIS DOES: tells you what a mining rock is worth BEFORE you crack it.
1. Scan a rock in game — your scanner shows its size (mass/SCU) and what's inside (e.g. "Quantanium 12%").
2. Type the rock size into ROCK SIZE above.

Tablet Capabilities
Everything CmdGlas can do, and how. It runs on your own PC, reads your own files, and never writes to the game.
It Remembers
Your notes, lists and picks persistNotepad, gather list, buy list, blueprint selections and inventory are still there next session — and next patch.
Everything is cross-pageSend blueprints from Blueprints and they appear in Craft Calculator and Operation. One store, many views — nothing is typed twice.
PC and iPad buildsThe same tablet, sized for each: the iPad keeps 44px tap targets and its own notch handling.
Cross-device syncNotes, gather and buy lists, craft picks, blueprints, reputation and inventory move between PC and iPad through the control server on your own machine. Zoom and theme stay per-device on purpose — the iPad wants its own. Verified end-to-end 2026-07-16.
It Reads Your Actual Setup
Your real keybindsRead from the profile Star Citizen itself exports — not a list someone typed. Whatever you bound is what it shows.
Your joystick binds tooHOTAS bindings are read alongside keyboard. Your rudder, throttle and stick are not invisible here.
Your devices, discoveredVKB, VIRPIL, Logitech, Thrustmaster, anything — the game names them in its own export, so there is no vendor list to fall out of date.
Peripheral profiles, regeneratedStream Deck, VoiceAttack and Azeron import files are rebuilt from your newest export, so they follow your binds instead of drifting from them.
It Stays Current
The live patch, derivedThe build number comes from the live feed, not a value somebody remembered to update.
Live commodity pricesPulled from UEX, with the age of every price shown so you can judge it.
It tells you what it doesn't knowEvery claim is tagged VERIFIED, COMMUNITY or UNCONFIRMED, and stamped with the patch it was confirmed on. Confidence is a feature; false confidence is a bug.
It Stays Out Of The Way
Pop-out overlayA floating always-on-top window on a second monitor — craft list, notepad, inventory, mining reference, and a mini Operation panel, all fed from the main tablet.
Basic or ExpertRead the field manual, or the full tables. Your choice, per page.
Yours to arrangeTen colourways, per-page zoom, draggable Operation panels. It should look how you want at 2am.
It Doesn't Touch Your Game
Read-only where it countsIt will not add to or change your game files. Your in-game keybind list is never edited. Verified against this app's own source code, not merely promised.
You choose what it buildsThe only files it ever creates are peripheral binding profiles, in their own folders, when you ask. Mouse and keyboard only? Tick nothing and it writes nothing at all.
Nothing that trips anti-cheatNo injection, no overlay hooks, no automation of the game. It is a second screen reading a file.
A Different Job To mobiGlas
mobiGlas lives inside the fictionIt is in the game, in-universe, on a wrist, with an immersion budget and a ship date. That is a genuinely harder brief than this one.
This lives on your deskA second screen has no immersion to protect and no lore to obey. It can be a spreadsheet when a spreadsheet is what you want — and it can stay open while you fly.
So they are not competingThis exists to do the paperwork, so the mobiGlas can stay the thing you use in the cockpit. If CIG ever ships this in-game, that is a good day — it means nobody needs a second screen.
The honest part. Almost everything above is built on the outside: files the game writes on your PC, a community wiki API, and prices other players typed in. There is no official Star Citizen API to ask, so nothing here is fed by the game directly — which is exactly why every figure carries a source tag instead of a confident face.

That is not a complaint. It is the reason this tablet is careful, and the reason it will always tell you when it is guessing. The full picture — and what would make it better — is on the Starmap page.

On an iPad or Android tablet. CmdGlas can show on a tablet, but the PC serves it first: run the control-server .bat once and open the address it prints from your tablet's browser. Step-by-step instructions are in the USER GUIDE (top bar, between the zoom slider and the clock).
DO NOT SUBMIT, PROMOTE OR DISTRIBUTE GLITCHES, CHEATS AND EXPLOITS — verified legitimate fixes and techniques only.
TROUBLESHOOTING
Pick an activity. Every tip is tagged VERIFIED (CIG says so) · COMMUNITY (players found it) · UNCONFIRMED — and stamped with the patch it was confirmed on, because tips rot.
SHOW STOPPERS
The current top progression-blocking bugs in Alpha 4.9, from CIG’s official Known Issues list (last updated 16 Jul 2026, build 4.9.0-LIVE). Each names the loop it breaks and any known workaround. Open CIG’s live Known Issues ↗ — always check there for the newest, since this list is a stamped snapshot.
1 Inventory items silently swapped for fire extinguishers CONFIRMED
Blocks: any loop — inventory, loadout, consumables
After the patch, random items in your inventory can turn into fire extinguishers, wiping gear you needed before you even start an activity.
Workaround: None yet — CIG is still collecting data (Issue Council STARC-214845).
2 Inventory and hand-held items lost after the patch CONFIRMED
Blocks: any loop — inventory persistence
Items disappear (including anything held in-hand at logout). Losses can be large and CIG Support cannot restore them.
Workaround: Items held in hand are sometimes recoverable from your hab bed; otherwise none (STARC-194626).
3 Refinery work orders won’t start at the kiosk CONFIRMED
Blocks: mining / refining — the payout step
The quotation panel vanishes and the refining order won’t begin, so mined ore can’t be processed or sold.
Workaround: Move your ore pods into local inventory first, then start the order (instead of pulling from the stored ship).
4 Mining gadgets won’t deploy while in EVA CONFIRMED
Blocks: hand / FPS mining
Consumable mining gadgets can’t be placed during EVA, blocking optimal rock cracking. Patch notes list this as fixed, but players report it still happening.
Workaround: None.
5 Rented ships don’t appear at ASOP terminals CONFIRMED
Blocks: ship claiming / rentals — getting into a ship at all
Rental ships fail to show at the terminal, so you can’t spawn them to begin any loop.
Workaround: Restart your router and flush your DNS.
6 Storing a ship at Area18 traps you in “Repositioning Player” CONFIRMED
Blocks: ship storage / station turnaround
Storing at the Area18 ASOP can lock you in a stuck state where Backspace and respawn stop responding.
Workaround: Exit to the main menu and rejoin.
7 Repair / Refuel / Restock missing at service points CONFIRMED
Blocks: resupply — gating cargo, combat and mining runs
The service options don’t appear in your mobiGlas, so you can’t rearm, refuel or repair to keep going.
Workaround: Wait for the hangar doors to close, then close and reopen mobiGlas; or wait a few minutes after landing and reopen the Landing Services app.
8 Some ships never finish repairs after losing thrusters CONFIRMED
Blocks: ship maintenance / repair
Ships that lose a thruster (with landing gear beneath it) can get stuck on “processing” forever, leaving the ship unrepairable.
Workaround: None once it happens — only prevention.
9 “Repel Raid on Orison” enemies don’t spawn CONFIRMED
Blocks: missions / bounties (Crusader Security)
The enemies never appear, so the mission can’t be finished — and abandoning it damages your Crusader Security reputation.
Workaround: Don’t accept this mission.
10 “Evict Illegal Occupants” targets don’t spawn CONFIRMED
Blocks: missions (derelict outpost contracts)
The occupants you’re sent to clear never spawn, so the contract can’t be completed.
Workaround: None.
All ten are on CIG’s official Known Issues list CONFIRMED. There is no public bug-tracker feed to pull live (the Issue Council needs a sign-in), so this is a hand-checked snapshot — flag it for an update after a new patch or hotfix.
COMMUNITY FIX — 4.9 RECO SCANNING CONTRACT
A community-reported progression bug that is not on CIG’s official Known Issues list. Found and explained by MrKraken. Watch MrKraken’s video ↗
! RECO scanning contract won’t register the scan COMMUNITY
Blocks: RECO research / scanning contracts
The new auto-scan-on-ping feature can fail to register when you are close to the target asteroid cluster, leaving the contract stuck with no completion (a server desync). Per MrKraken.
Workaround — do in order:

1. Within 10 km of the cluster, switch out of scan or mining mode so you don’t trigger an auto-scan.

2. If the hint pop-up doesn’t appear within 5 minutes, untrack the contract, then re-track it.

3. If it still fails, change server shards (relog to a fresh shard).

NOTE: the 10 km and 5-minute figures are MrKraken’s, from his video. No danger to your account — all three are normal in-game actions.

YOUR BUILD
TEXT & LOCALIZATION TOOLS (OPTIONAL, FREE)
Both tools below only edit Star Citizen’s on-screen text (the localization file the game reads). They run offline, do not inject into or overlay the game, and use the customization CIG has said is intended / allowed — so they are not the kind of tool anti-cheat targets. Neither touches your account or ship data.
SMART CITIZEN — LOCALIZATION EDITOR
A free desktop app that edits the game’s text: rename missions, show real reputation ranks instead of “Tier 1”, and clean up labels. It edits the localization file only — no injection, no overlay.
GET IT
SMART CITIZEN · RELEASES ↗ grab the newest version at the top
INSTALL & USE
1. Open the Releases page above (link).

2. Download the newest release. Two choices: the portable ZIP (no installer) or the Setup .exe.

3. NOTE: the app is unsigned (free side-project). Windows 11 Smart App Control may block the .exe. The portable ZIP avoids this — use it if you’d rather not change any Windows setting.

4. CAUTION: only turn Smart App Control off if you understand it lowers a Windows security guard — turn it back on afterward. Prefer the portable ZIP.

5. Launch Smart Citizen.

6. Go to the Config tab and click Extract from Data.p4k to load the game’s stock text.

7. Search for the text you want to change, double-click the Custom Value column, and type your replacement.

8. Click Apply to Game — it writes the localization file and makes an automatic backup.

9. Re-apply after each SC patch (the game resets its text every build).
MRKRAKEN STARSTRINGS — READY-MADE TEXT PACK
MrKraken’s ready-made set of text replacements — a community quality-of-life pack that relabels confusing in-game text for you. Same localization system as Smart Citizen; no editing required, just drop it in.
GET IT
STARSTRINGS · GITHUB ↗
INSTALL
1. Open the StarStrings GitHub page above (link).

2. Download the latest release (right-hand side of the page).

3. Extract the ZIP.

4. NOTE: if you already have a user.cfg in your game’s LIVE folder, do not overwrite it — open your existing one and add this line at the end:
g_language = english

5. Copy the data folder and the user.cfg into your game’s LIVE folder root:
...\StarCitizen\LIVE\  (holds user.cfg + data\Localization\english\global.ini)

6. Launch the game.

7. NOTE: check for an updated StarStrings after every patch — the game’s text changes each build and a stale file can show blank labels. MrKraken re-publishes it each patch.

MEDICAL FIELD MANUAL NEW
Pens · MedGun · LifeGuard · MedBeds · respawn · blood drug level · refills · prices — Alpha 4.9. Every figure is sourced and tagged; unconfirmed items are flagged. Prices drift — confirm in-game.
TREATMENT TIERS — READ FIRST
A bed or facility must MATCH OR EXCEED the injury tier for a full cure. A lower tier only stabilises you for transport. [VERIFIED]

T3 — MINOR: damaged limbs, reduced max-health states. [VERIFIED]
T2 — MODERATE: ruined limbs, multiple limb bleed-outs (limb restoration). [VERIFIED]
T1 — SEVERE: near-death and fatal injuries (full revival). Highest tier. [VERIFIED]
MEDPENS & DRUG PENS
All are CureLife single-use injectors (not refillable — re-buy or loot). [VERIFIED]

MedPen (Hemozal) — heals, stops bleeding, revives from incapacitated. Raises Blood Drug Level +30. [VERIFIED]

DetoxPen (Resurgera) — reverses an overdose (only if not injury-incapacitated); DOUBLES blood-drug decay. This is your blood-drug-level reducer. [VERIFIED]

AdrenaPen (Demexatrine) — clears concussion symptoms; restores weapon handling and move speed. (Your “Adrenaline”.) [VERIFIED]

CorticoPen (Sterogen) — clears vision/hearing symptoms; restores stamina. [VERIFIED]

OpioPen (Roxaphen) — clears pain symptoms; restores movement. [VERIFIED]

DeconPen (Canoiodide) — reduces radiation injuries. (Your “Deconot”; the drug is Canoiodide.) [VERIFIED]

OxyPen — emergency suit oxygen; no blood-drug impact. [COMMUNITY]

CAP COLOURS: the pens are colour-coded in-game, but no text source documents the exact colour per drug. Read the printed NAME on the pen, not the colour. [UNCONFIRMED]
BLOOD DRUG LEVEL (BDL) — HOW TO LOWER IT
Every drug pen raises BDL. Rising BDL = slower movement, blurred vision, weapon sway, erratic piloting. At 100% you OVERDOSE and take damage. [VERIFIED]

BDL decays on its own over time. [VERIFIED]

TO LOWER IT FAST: DetoxPen (Resurgera) doubles the decay rate. [VERIFIED]
The MedGun (ParaMed) can also inject Resurgera. The LifeGuard multitool attachment CANNOT — it delivers Hemozal only. [VERIFIED]
MEDGUN — ParaMed Medical Device
CureLife, Size 1 handheld. Heals 10 HP/sec at 1.5 m range and shows patient vitals. [VERIFIED]

Injects: Hemozal, Roxaphen, Demexatrine, Sterogen, Resurgera. [VERIFIED]

Holds 200 charges. REFILL: MedGel Refill vial into the S1 ParaMed refill port. [VERIFIED]

Price ~1,426–1,500 aUEC. Buy at pharmacies: New Babbage, Area 18, Lorville, ARC-L1, ARC-L4. [VERIFIED]
MULTITOOL MEDICAL ATTACHMENT — LifeGuard
Greycat attachment for the multitool. Heals players/NPCs at a distance with Hemozal ONLY. [VERIFIED]

VS the MedGun: LifeGuard shows NO vitals, delivers NO drug pens, and CANNOT detox. Use the ParaMed MedGun when you need drugs or vitals. [VERIFIED]

Price ~333–350 aUEC (cheapest: Maria Pure of Heart, Lorville). [VERIFIED]

REFILL: LifeGuard Refill vial (300 units), ~119–125 aUEC, sold at 50+ locations. [VERIFIED]
MEDBEDS & RESPAWN

SETTINGS & CURVES — FLIGHT TIPS
General setup method — exact curve values depend on your hardware + feel. Community-sourced, verified 2026-07-14.
Deadzone — set only as much as needed so the axis rests at true center when released. Stiff spring / hard cam needs less; soft spring needs more.
Don't stack deadzones — if your VKB/VIRPIL/brand software already applies a deadzone, set the in-game deadzone to 0 (and vice-versa).
Curves / exponent — add an exponential response curve to soften the center for fine aim while keeping full deflection at the edges. Start subtle, raise to taste.
Saturation — if the gimbal can't reach software max travel, lower saturation; raise deadzone until it always reports center at rest.
Bind only the axes you need — pitch, yaw, roll + strafe (fwd/back, left/right). Everything else goes on buttons.
ESP (Enhanced Stick Precision) — SC's fine-aim assist near a target. Tune your sensitivity curve alongside it, not against it.
HOSAS vs HOTAS — dual sticks (HOSAS) give full 6DOF strafe; HOTAS leans on throttle-managed flight. Bind to match your layout.
Save on-device — VIRPIL / VKB / Azeron store profiles on the hardware, so binds survive a PC swap.
Tools: SC Launch Configurator (community, advanced per-axis curves) · Windows joy.cpl to confirm the OS sees full travel.
STAR CITIZEN CONTROL MAPPING
SC's keybindings live inside the game — no web link or URL can open them. Set bindings here:
Options → Keybindings → Advanced Controls Customization → [device / category]
To save or move a binding profile, SC reads/writes XML in this folder on the PC:
…\StarCitizen\LIVE\USER\Client\0\Controls\Mappings
In-game console (`): pp_rebindkeys export <name> writes the XML there; pp_rebindkeys <name> loads it back.
CRAFTING — FIELD MANUAL
HOW TO READ THIS. Crafting is new and CIG has published no 4.8-era guide. Their only official write-up is 4.7. So every line below is tagged: VERIFIED = official/primary source · COMMUNITY = credible but unofficial · UNCONFIRMED = nobody publishes it; do not bet aUEC on it.
A. THE LOOP
1. Buy an Item Fabricator (see C). Pull it from hangar storage at the freight console — search “FAB”. [COMMUNITY]

2. Move it with a tractor beam. It attaches to cargo grids, so it can ride in a ship. Placed in your hangar, it also reads your local inventory directly. [VERIFIED — CIG]

3. Get the materials into LOCAL INVENTORY. If they aren't there, the fabricator cannot see them. This is the #1 reason a new crafter thinks the machine is broken. [VERIFIED — CIG]

4. Pick a blueprint, assign materials (there are autofill / best / worst buttons), watch the live stat preview, choose a delivery location, hit Fabricate. [VERIFIED — CIG]

5. Crafting and dismantling run separate simultaneous queues; finished jobs land in a history log. [VERIFIED — CIG]

Blueprints are account-bound and permanent once acquired — they survive death. From mission rewards (low drop rate), reputation, loot crates, or purchase. [VERIFIED — CIG]
Craft times and any aUEC job fee: [UNCONFIRMED] — CIG says only that time scales with size and quality. No source publishes real numbers.
B. BIG ITEMS — SHIP COMPONENTS & SHIP WEAPONS
WHERE A FINISHED ITEM GOES: a completed craft is deposited into your LOCAL INVENTORY at the station or planet where you crafted it (the delivery location you chose). You do not carry it out of the fabricator by hand. [COMMUNITY — player-reported; confirm in-game]
Getting a large item out:

1. Open your LOCAL INVENTORY at that station / planet.

2. Withdraw the item. A ship component or weapon withdraws onto a ship’s cargo grid through the freight elevator — the same path as any oversized item you buy. [COMMUNITY]

What is confirmed:

• Ship-component and ship-weapon blueprints DO exist in 4.8, datamined straight from the game files. [COMMUNITY — RSI Community Hub blueprint finder, 4.8 files]

• The fabricator has its own internal cargo grid “for the input and output of resources and items.” [VERIFIED — CIG, direct quote]

Not documented — do not assume:

• No size or SCU limit on crafted items is published anywhere — the string “SCU” does not appear in CIG’s crafting guide. [UNCONFIRMED]

There is no personal-vs-industrial fabricator split in LIVE. One machine exists. Food, Medical and Construction fabricators are explicitly in development — the Construction one, at hangar scale, is what will craft ships. In-vehicle crafting machines are also in development. [VERIFIED — CIG]
C. WHERE TO BUY A FABRICATOR
One model exists: the RediMake Item Fabricator (KE Group). There are no fabricator tiers. [VERIFIED]
Average ~99,771 aUEC across 22 terminals. [COMMUNITY — UEX, 4.8.x]

CHEAPEST: 95,001 aUEC — Tammany and Sons, Metro Center, Lorville (Hurston). Only 4.8.3-stamped price on the board.
• 99,990 — Kel-To, Aspire Grand, New Babbage (microTech); Refinery Shop ARC-L1; Refinery Shop HUR-L1
• 100,000 — Dumper's Depot Area 18, and most Refinery Shops / Pyro / Nyx terminals

CAUTION — RESALE: the only sell-back seen is 35,980 aUEC at MIC-L1. That's roughly a 64% loss. Buy it once, in the right place. [COMMUNITY — UEX]

WARNING — THE 100K TRAP: a fabricator left deployed can disappear from your hangar. Stow it on the freight elevator when you're done. Widely reported. [COMMUNITY]
D. ORE QUALITY → GEAR QUALITY
CORRECTION — this tablet previously had this wrong. The bands are driven by the ore's QUALITY value, not its DENSITY. Density isn't even a per-rock stat — a rock's stats are Mass, Instability and Resistance. “Density” in mining talk means how concentrated a material is at a location. The old “not resistance” half was right; the “density” half was a conflation.
Every resource carries a quality value 0–1000, and that value determines the traits of anything crafted from it. [VERIFIED — CIG, direct quote]
Quality can only be read up close in mining mode — rock type scans from range, quality does not. [COMMUNITY]
Refining preserves quality. Mixing qualities averages the finished item. [VERIFIED — CIG]

THE 8 BANDS — ore in a band all snaps to the same quality value: [COMMUNITY — Scopique, reporting 4.8 PTU notes]
BandSource rangeSnaps to (IRON)
10–399325
2400–599521
3600–699664
4700–799710
5800–899874
6900–949907
7950–998970
8999–10001000
TWO CAVEATS OR THIS TABLE WILL MISLEAD YOU:
1. These snap values are IRON-specific. The rule says each ore type has its own value per band, so copper's band 2 is probably NOT 521. A per-ore table does not exist publicly. [UNCONFIRMED]
2. The source is a blog reporting leaked 4.8 PTU notes — not CIG, and not confirmed against 4.8 LIVE. [UNCONFIRMED vs LIVE]
E. WHAT BANDS FOR MAX GEAR
q500 is the break-even. At 500 your crafted item matches what you'd buy off an NPC shelf. Below 500 you get penalties; above 500, bonuses. [COMMUNITY] — note the number 500 appears nowhere in CIG's own guide; this is community-derived.

Worked example (P4-AR + iron): q325 → −2.62% impact, −4.2% fire rate. q710 → +3.15% impact, +5.84% fire rate. [COMMUNITY — 4.7 data]

MAX GEAR = BAND 8 (999–1000). No cap is documented — higher appears to be better all the way to 1000. [UNCONFIRMED that any cap exists]

THE THING THAT ACTUALLY CHANGES HOW YOU MINE (synthesis, not a sourced claim):
The bands create hard plateaus. A q899 rock and a q800 rock both snap to 874 — identical gear. So quality gained within a band is worth nothing. The only thing that pays is crossing into the next band.
And the bands collapse at the top: Band 1 spans 400 points; Band 8 spans 2. Band 8 will be brutally rare — chasing it is a lottery, while Band 4 (700+) is the realistic target for good gear.
Rules of thumb: most rocks land 200–600; Stanton commonly 350–450; Pyro runs better; 800+ is rare and 900+ takes serious dedication. [COMMUNITY]
F. TRAPS & THINGS THAT AREN'T IN YET
• Dismantling returns shop/loot items at default quality 500. Player-crafted items return the quality you built them with, but less of it — material is lost in manufacture and teardown. This is the only waste mechanic. [VERIFIED — CIG]

• Variant gear generally can't be dismantled — basic/non-variant only. [COMMUNITY]

• Craft failure chance: no source mentions any. [UNCONFIRMED]

• Crafted-gear persistence / insurance: CIG documents this for blueprints only. Gear is [UNCONFIRMED]. Note 4.8.0 shipped a full character wipe, the first since 4.0. [VERIFIED]

• NOT IN THE GAME YET (all future-tense in CIG's guide): item degradation & repair, catalysts, blueprint tiers & research (T1–3, vehicles to T5), datapad blueprints, a blueprint library app, player trading of materials, the new alloy/byproduct refining system, salvage integration. [VERIFIED — CIG]

• CIG's own hedge: “blueprint requirements are subject to change in future patches.” [VERIFIED]
YOU CAN CLOSE THE BIGGEST GAP YOURSELF. One screenshot of the fabricator's “delivery location” dropdown would settle the big-item question that no source on the internet currently answers. Snap it and this manual gets a verified section B.
